# CANDIDATE: VWAP_DEVIATION_RIBBON_MEANREVERSION

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis
Price tends to revert to VWAP when extended beyond 1 ATR while the EMA ribbon is flat, indicating lack of trend. This mean-reversion edge exists because extended deviations from VWAP in low-trend environments (flat ribbon) are statistically likely to revert as the market seeks equilibrium, unlike trending regimes where ribbon slope exceeds 0.1%.

## Mechanism
Calculate 20-period EMA, 50-period EMA, 200-period EMA (ribbon). If the absolute difference between close and VWAP exceeds 1*ATR(14) AND the ribbon slope (20 EMA minus 50 EMA) is within +/-0.05% of price (near flat) AND volume > 1.5*average volume(20), then enter long if close < VWAP, short if close > VWAP. Exit shape: Initial stop at the opposite side of the deviation band (long: stop at VWAP + 1*ATR; short: stop at VWAP - 1*ATR). Take profit at 1.5R or when price crosses VWAP (mean reversion complete). Use chart-stop if price makes a new swing opposite direction. Regime hint: Works best when VIX between 12-22 (moderate volatility) and time after 10:00 EST to avoid opening noise; avoid strong trending days where ribbon slope >0.1%.
